title: Optimization idea: Split file by media query(s).
impact: 2021 idea, 2 +1; one 2026 comment wants print styles split out. No duplicates found. Output splitting into multiple files is a bundler/HTML concern (Parcel/Vite emit the <link media> tags), not something transform() can express (single output).
summary: Request: split a stylesheet into one file per media query so bundlers can emit <link media=...> (non-render-blocking when not matching). Concerns raised: more requests, delayed styles on media change, cascade order changes (mischnic). Non-matching media stylesheets are still downloaded, so the gain is only render-blocking. Doable in userland today with the visitor API; a built-in would need a new multi-output API and careful handling of order, @layer order, nesting and @import.
repro: 28-repro.mjs pins a userland workaround: pass 1 transform() with targets {chrome:100} lowers nested `@media print`; pass 2 transform() with a StyleSheet visitor keeps/drops top-level `@media print`. Outputs: `.foo{color:#639}.bar{margin:0}` and `@media print{.foo{color:#000}.bar{display:none}}`. Correct on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1.
evidence: repro.mjs run on local + latest 3 releases. Note: StyleSheet visitors run before nesting lowering, so a single pass doesn't see nested @media at top level (verified: single-pass split left `@media print{.foo{...}}` in the screen part).

fix.approach: If wanted: a bundler option returning multiple outputs keyed by media query, with rules kept after the base sheet in original order; unsafe with @layer ordering and layered/imported CSS. Otherwise close, pointing to the visitor workaround and bundler plugins.

draftReply:
Thanks for the idea! It doesn't really fit transform(), which produces a single output, and splitting changes rule order, which can change the cascade. A bundler that writes the <link media> tags is a better place for it. You can already do this with the visitor API. Run transform() once with targets that lower nesting, so nested `@media print` blocks become top-level rules. Then run a second pass with a `StyleSheet` visitor that keeps only, or drops, the top-level `@media print` rules. Load the print file after the main one so the order stays the same. Be careful with `@layer`, since splitting can change layer order.
